title: The Week the Federal Epstein Case Changed Course: July 19–31, 2007
scope: A source-bound chronology of the July 19–31, 2007 shift toward a state-based resolution of the federal Epstein investigation, with the unresolved basis for the exact two-year term identified as the decision-record gap.

sources.supports: July 19 hold-off account; July 26 announcement account; July 31 term-sheet account; later explanation of internal disagreements.
sources.limit: Prepared in 2019; later recollection must be distinguished from contemporaneous records.

sources.supports: Contemporaneous document chronology: July 19 target-letter chains, July 26 indictment-change email, July 31 proposed plea terms and subsequent negotiations.
sources.limit: Privilege log describes documents but does not disclose their full privileged content.

sources.record: DOJ Office of Professional Responsibility Report on the Epstein investigation
sources.supports: OPR witness reconciliation; finding that Acosta ultimately made the two-year resolution decision; inability to identify contemporaneous basis/initial proposer of exact two-year term; no professional misconduct/improper motive evidence; poor-judgment conclusion.
sources.limit: Retrospective investigative report synthesizing records and interviews.

sources.record: DOJ OPR executive summary / public findings
sources.supports: Official summary of OPR conclusions regarding Acosta's authority, absence of professional misconduct/improper motive evidence, and poor-judgment finding.
sources.limit: Summary; full factual detail is in the full report.

sources.record: Terms of Epstein Non-Prosecution Agreement, July 31, 2007
sources.supports: Opening state-resolution terms presented July 31: state guilty pleas, at least two years, offender registration, victim damages mechanism, closure of federal investigation after plea/sentence.
sources.limit: Opening term sheet, not the final September 24 NPA.

open_questions: Who first proposed the exact two-year term of incarceration.
What contemporaneous analysis, if any, justified selecting two years rather than another term.
Whether the full unredacted July 19 management response and related July 26 decision communications can be publicly recovered.
What additional oral discussions between July 19 and July 26 informed the decision.
not_established: That the July 19 hold instruction itself came from Acosta.
That the two-year decision had already been made on July 19.
That the missing contemporaneous rationale proves corruption, favoritism, political influence or another improper motive.
That the July 31 term sheet was identical to the final September 24 NPA.
Professional misconduct by Acosta or the other subjects; OPR expressly did not find it.
